attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Priya Patel, MD
Department: Neonatology
Visit Type: inpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Excessive crying and irritability in newborn

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The mother reports that the baby has had difficulty sleeping and seems to be feeding poorly. She also notes that the baby's cry is high-pitched and that he has been sneezing frequently. The mother has a history of heroin use but states she has been in a methadone maintenance program for the past year.

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal opioid use disorder (heroin; currently enrolled in methadone maintenance program)
- Maternal chronic pain syndrome managed with long-term prescription opioids during pregnancy

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: Neonate.

VITAL SIGNS:
His temperature is 37.8°C (100°F), heart rate is 160 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 60 breaths per minute, and blood pressure is 65/40 mmHg. The neonate's birth weight was 3200 grams, and he has lost 5% of his body weight since birth.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the neonate is noted to have tremors, increased muscle tone, and tachypnea. The rest of the physical examination is unremarkable.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory Values:
- Complete Blood Count (CBC) within normal limits
- Serum electrolytes within normal limits
- Blood glucose: 75 mg/dL
- Urine toxicology screen: Positive for opiates

attachments.title: Source clinical note
attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-02-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Rodriguez, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Excessive crying and irritability for the past 24 hours

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns to the emergency department one month following a prior inpatient neonatology admission for similar symptoms. The mother reports that the baby is difficult to console, has a high-pitched cry, and seems to be feeding poorly. She denies any fever or respiratory symptoms in the neonate.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Neonatal Abstinence Syndrome (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal opioid use disorder (heroin; currently enrolled in methadone maintenance program)
- Maternal chronic pain syndrome managed with long-term prescription opioids during pregnancy

SOCIAL HISTORY:
The mother has a history of chronic pain and admits to using prescribed oxycodone throughout her pregnancy.

VITAL SIGNS:
His vital signs are as follows: temperature 37.2°C, heart rate 160 beats per minute, respiratory rate 60 breaths per minute, and blood pressure 65/40 mmHg.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the neonate is noted to have increased muscle tone, generalized tremors, and an exaggerated Moro reflex.

LABORATORY DATA:
Urine toxicology screen of the neonate returns positive for opioids.
